existing_tips: 'En fait' = actually / in fact. Very useful connector for correcting or clarifying what you just sai
Near future: aller + infinitive. Je vais manger = I'm going to eat. Very common at A1, often preferr
'L'' replaces 'le/la' before vowels or silent 'h': 'l'hôtel', 'l'aéroport'. Mandatory elision.
'Ça fait longtemps' = It's been a while. 'Ça fait + time' expresses duration: Ça fait deux ans = It'
'Salut' is informal for both 'hi' and 'bye'. 'Ça va ?' is the casual way to ask 'how are you?'
'Il y a' = there is / there are. Works for both singular and plural. 'Il y a du monde' = there are p
'Pour emporter' = to go / takeaway. 'Sur place' = to eat in. Common at restaurants and cafés.
Dates: le + number + month. 'Le premier' for the 1st, then cardinal numbers: le deux, le trois. Mont
'Avoir horreur de' = to hate/detest something. An avoir expression: J'ai horreur du lundi = I hate M
'Arrête de' + infinitive = stop doing something. 'Commence à' + infinitive = start doing something.
